claims: HBCUs are accredited institutions established before 1964 to provide higher education to African Americans.
Over 100 HBCUs operate in the U.S.
HBCUs operate primarily in the South.
HBCUs produce 20% of Black graduates.
Howard University is in DC.
Spelman College is in GA.
Morehouse College is in GA.
Hampton University is in VA.
Howard University is frequently ranked #1.
Spelman College has a ~23% acceptance rate.
There are over 100 HBCUs in the United States.
HBCUs include public and private four-year institutions.
HBCUs include two-year colleges.
HBCUs were founded in the 19th and early 20th centuries.
The Searchable Museum notes that HBCUs were established to provide education to people of African descent, particularly in the South, when they were otherwise denied access to higher education.
Martin Luther King Jr. is an alumnus of Morehouse College.
Toni Morrison is an alumnus of Howard University.
Spike Lee is an alumnus of Morehouse College.
Vice President Kamala Harris is an alumnus of Howard University.
US News & World Report ranks Howard University among the top 10 HBCUs.
US News & World Report ranks Spelman College among the top 10 HBCUs.
US News & World Report ranks Hampton University among the top 10 HBCUs.
US News & World Report ranks Morehouse College among the top 10 HBCUs.
US News & World Report ranks Xavier University of Louisiana among the top 10 HBCUs.
Florida A&M University is a top school among HBCUs
